scenes.heading: TLS
scenes.caption: TLS is the protocol that encrypts a connection, usually seen as HTTPS. It also lets the client check it is talking to the real server, via a certificate. Without it, anyone on the path can read or change the traffic, including passwords and tokens.

scenes.heading: Logging
scenes.caption: Logging is writing a record of what the program did, so you can reconstruct a failure later. A useful log names the request, the decision, and the error. A useless log is either silent or a firehose of noise nobody reads.
